Independent source-scope review of PR559 for the mixed PR558-derived complex cover
Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. 2026-10-12 UTC.

Conclusion

The native exact-complex moment is conditionally justified for mixed template
625590098a4c2bd3d0da9c78262a53c486a240477cb8348219bd4512f573edfc.
The PR559 reasoning applies to this actual two-provider controller, provided the
same inherited all-size exact-complex compiler and outer-transfer contracts are
retained. The bit bad-residue surcharge must remain. This is not a new proof of
those inherited contracts and is not an unconditional multiplication theorem.

Why the two recurrence terms differ

The original complex cover uses a finite binary orthogonal group. Exact
Gaussian-dyadic Clifford representatives exist for every selected binary frame;
each nested frame transition lowers to finite rank-zero adapters surrounding its
single paid coordinate Fourier child. Endpoint and dirty-tail identities are
operator equalities, including exact phases, rather than success statements on
a subset of residue classes. The full orthogonal-cover multiplicity cancels from
the normalized child moment, but remains fully charged in the finite invoice.

The adjacent bit construction instead has width-dependent GL_m(R_w) selectors.
It proves good-class whole-rank execution and a real local-ring fallback on a
small exceptional residue fraction. The bound adds 32*m^2 rank-one fallback
children on a 10^-16 fraction of each ideal edge. This separate bit obligation
is not created merely because fixed binary GL matrices are used to choose exact
complex Clifford representatives.

The conservative assembly used the same bad=True arithmetic helper for both
suppliers, thereby adding that bit fallback to the already exhaustive complex
profile. Under the exact-complex compiler contract, it is sufficient to charge

    sum_r H[r] * (r/73)^(1-b) / 7168.

Only the extra complex fallback term is omitted. No paid child, idle remainder,
Clifford adapter, scalar/Horner primitive, wrapper, group router, precision,
tape, external-row or all-size obligation is omitted.

Transfer to the actual mixed controller

Both selected providers have been independently replayed on all 728 arbitrary
scalar columns in both reflected orientations, including all 504 dirty helper
columns and private-work erasure. Their native event lists, actual local paid
profiles, phase recipes and normalization adapters are bound into the emitted
provider registry. Exactly 71 calls use rank5_eight and only (stage 4, replica 6)
uses coldkernel000. The call, sweep, orientation and program hashes agree.
Provider selection does not depend on the cover group element or on a residue
class. Every cover vertex uses the same finite schedule and selected programs.

The independent controller audit reconstructed all 36,288 helper owner roles,
including availability windows through individual bridges, one whole physical
owner per helper invocation, disjoint residual slots, actual spectator axes,
3,178 orthogonal 73-column chart types, and all 4,368 positive idle remainders.
Its complete profile is:

 {1:166881, 2:30530, 3:35777, 4:13824, 5:4032, 6:4032,
  7:208, 8:576, 40:1, 48:1660}.

Each fixed orthogonal owner chart acts by right translation on the full retained
cover group; right translation is a bijection. This supplies the same complete
construction at every group vertex. Different fixed providers at different
schedule positions do not introduce an exceptional subset. No enumeration of
the enormous entire orthogonal group is claimed: the finite chart checks and
exact group-translation argument are distinct parts of the reasoning.

The fresh mixed finite invoice recounts actual selected-provider scalar/Horner
work and wrappers, uses conservative shared compiler maxima, and retains the
full group stock and router charge. All nine finite checks pass; prefix 225 is
below payload 512, physical row coefficient 16,467 is below 20,161, and the
halving check is 73^2 = 5,329 > 2*48^2 = 4,608. Those guards are unchanged by the
recurrence correction.

Independent exact arithmetic

The two rational engines give the accepted supplier endpoint
 b = 0.001595058893494095255548
and reject b + 10^-24. The old contaminated complex model rejects the new
endpoint, demonstrating that the numerical difference is precisely a recurrence
choice and not a hidden change to source or owners. With the unchanged cited
PR543 bit cap c = 0.001653826988146798944268, including its fallback term, six
bootstrap levels and all 47 strict outer inequalities yield
 kappa = 0.001592518732327041.
The next 10^-18 kappa grid point is rejected by that assembly witness.
The gain over the conservative mixed kappa 0.001592518729588709 is 2.738332e-12.
RESULT.json retains the exact rational intervals, inequalities and source hashes.

Required conditions and limits

1. Completed recursive children must implement the exact Gaussian-dyadic complex
   operators on all roles under the inherited all-size compiler/common-label
   interface; the finite replay does not prove arbitrary-size realization.
2. Selected providers must remain fixed per complete invocation and uniformly
   transported across the complete finite orthogonal cover. A new provider with
   actual exceptional residue classes would require a new fallback analysis.
3. Dirty restoration, both reflected scalar/frame ledgers, exact Clifford phases,
   wrapper normalization, complete paid profiles, owner windows and residual
   remainders remain admission requirements, all checked for this template.
4. Full finite group/router and literal scalar/Horner/adapter charges, completed
   call precision, fixed tape/exact recovery and external-row contracts remain.
5. The PR543 bit compiler, mutable-source/local-ring selector and H1-H5 conditions,
   including its complete bad-class fallback, remain separate assumptions.
6. The inherited analytic/outer transfer remains conditional. This review changes
   no operator and proves no unconditional theorem, practical speedup or general
   optimality claim. Published heads have not been edited.
